svg.text: Knowledge of private cloud operations management with VMware Cloud Foundation: 288 files, about 327K tokens. Bands: method and product, layers, slices of one fact, anatomy of a file, paths to the model.
Method explains how private cloud is managed. Product is the knowledge of the IT products involved. Each has supporting files, drawn with a dashed outline.
The SP5 Framework: how private cloud is managed, with VCF terms and examples.
the framework across pillars: health check,
how to read telemetry: input types, interval,
KPI design, KPI vs SLA, noisy neighbour
supporting file: one English word per concept, other names
users say, confusable pairs such as Usage vs Utilization
VMware Cloud Foundation, Windows and Linux. Hardware appears as the physical layer under ESXi.
The product VCF Operations: its role, alert definitions,
report suite, dashboards and features as built.
Windows and Linux above the VM: a separate layer, not VMware
supporting files: exact values loaded into SQLite and looked up by key: vCenter counters, esxtop fields,
Tag: layer. A VM is a virtual motherboard and the Guest OS above it is a separate layer, so the layer that produces a metric decides its home.
Windows or Linux inside the VM
Not a Broadcom product, not part of the VM.
The VM as the hypervisor presents it
Example: vCPU Ready, the consumer view.
The provider view of the same resource.
Tag only: no folder of its own.
Vantage points: a consumer VM is seen from the virtual motherboard, and the provider ESXi from the hypervisor. The same word can mean different things in two layers.
Example: reading ESXi CPU Ready as the host waiting for CPU is wrong, because Ready is a consumer metric. The layer tag keeps the two apart in search.
The folder tree holds one slice. Tags and links hold the others. Retrieval filters on any tag, and the model follows any link.
One metric, one object type, one file. Kind: metric-meaning. Class: contention.
Listed in vm-health-check, part of the
the cluster KPI in the SP5 Framework.
Tags: scope, technology, pillar, product, object, layer, instance, metric_class. Links: internal_derive, same_name, same_meaning, related. Together they list which files are read together.
One fact per bullet, so a mistake sits on one line. Templates fix the section names, so one question finds the same section in every file.
What does this number mean on this object?
How does it work? Why does the metric behave so?
What to configure, which alerts, and why.
It is slow or down. Why? Order of checks.
Can it, should it, how much?
Is it healthy? What to check, in what order.
The harness reads the kind from the metadata.
A wrong reading in the user's words, and its fix.
Master of a flow; steps follow it.
A ## section is the unit of retrieval.
Links choose what is read together.
Vendor version, draft or reviewed, what to check.
The marked misconception goes with every question.
Five ways knowledge reaches the model: retrieved, looked up, given up front, run as code, set as agent instructions. Each fact has one home.
